Owners in the **Caribbean and Latin America** commonly look at brands that can signal **design-forward**, **boutique**, or **distinctive-character lifestyle** positioning, especially within the luxury/lifestyle segments.[5][6][15][17]

Brands most often associated with that positioning in the region include:

| Brand family | Why owners consider it for lifestyle/design-forward positioning | Evidence in the region |
|---|---|---|
| **JdV by Hyatt** | Known for an eclectic, locally rooted, design-driven style and “less rigid, more vibrant” guest experience | First Caribbean entry at Royal Beach Hotel Punta Cana[1][2][7] |
| **Kimpton** | Widely positioned as laid-back luxury with a strong lifestyle identity | Opened in Grand Cayman; also cited as a regionally expanding lifestyle brand[5][6][15] |
| **Hotel Indigo** | Neighborhood- and story-led boutique positioning, useful for distinctive local character | Highlighted by IHG as a “boutique neighborhood” concept in Mexico/LATAM/Caribbean[6] |
| **Vignette Collection** | Curated, one-of-a-kind independent-feeling luxury collection | Listed among IHG’s luxury/lifestyle brands expanding in the region[5][6] |
| **Curio Collection by Hilton** | Strong fit for independent, design-led hotels with local identity | Openings/signings across Medellín, Mexico, Colombia, Brazil, Dominican Republic, and more[3][17] |
| **Tapestry Collection by Hilton** | Also aimed at distinctive, locally inspired hotels | Mentioned in regional signings such as Bogotá and Suriname[3][17] |
| **Canopy by Hilton** | Lifestyle brand aimed at younger, more adventurous travelers | Cited as part of Hilton’s regional lifestyle expansion[17] |
| **The Luxury Collection** | Destination-driven luxury with a strong emphasis on place, culture, and refined design | Caribbean/LATAM presence highlighted with “authentic destination experiences” and design-forward retreats[9] |
| **Autograph Collection** | Independent-style branded hotels with strong individual identity | Mentioned as a Caribbean boutique/lifestyle option in regional development coverage[15] |
| **SLS** | High-energy, design-forward luxury lifestyle brand | Opened at Baha Mar in the Bahamas[4] |
| **Six Senses** | Wellness- and design-led luxury with distinctive character | Regional luxury/lifestyle expansion noted in Mexico, Latin America, and the Caribbean[5][6][13] |
| **Margaritaville** | Casual lifestyle resort branding with strong personality | Listed among brands expanding in the Caribbean[15] |

A few broader patterns stand out:

- **IHG** is explicitly marketing a luxury/lifestyle cluster in the region through **Six Senses, Regent, InterContinental, Vignette Collection, Kimpton, and Hotel Indigo**.[5][6]
- **Hilton** is growing its lifestyle footprint with **Curio Collection, Tapestry Collection, Canopy, and Conrad/Waldorf Astoria** in Caribbean and Latin American destinations.[3][17]
- **Hyatt**’s most clearly lifestyle-oriented play in the Caribbean is **JdV by Hyatt**, while its all-inclusive pipeline is broader and more resort-oriented.[1][7][14]
- **Marriott** owner interest often centers on **The Luxury Collection** and **Autograph Collection** when the goal is destination character and design-led differentiation.[9][15]

If you want, I can also turn this into a **shortlist by owner profile**—for example, *soft brand / independent conversion / upper-upscale resort / adults-only all-inclusive / urban lifestyle*.
